chapter: Oliver, Kelly and the district bands
title: Happy Galloway's band and country work
summary: Dawson played guitar with Galloway, a one-legged bass player and barber, whose band included Kid Punch, Frankie Dusen and Joe Welch.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well, you'd remember, uh, did you remember bands like the Galloway band?
Galloway, yes. I even played a couple jobs with them, with Galloway. I played guitar with Galloway. He was the one-legged bass player.

Yeah, he was the bass player. He had one leg walk with one crutch. Oh. Wasn't that Charlie Galloway, was it? Uh, yeah, I believe it was Charlie Galloway. I think that was his first name, Charlie Galloway.
I heard somebody call him Happy Galloway.

Oh, he had, uh, well, that was, uh, that was the name of the band, Happy Galloway's band. Oh, I see. Because, see, it was his band. It went by his name. He had a barber shop on here on, on Baltimore between Pardis and Lafayette. He had a barber shop.
Can you remember who was band?
Uh, he had, well, he had, um, he had, well, he first, when Kid Punch first came here from the country, the trumpet player, he had Kid Punch with him.
I didn't know that we see Punch all the time.
I don't remember that. Yeah, ask him. Just ask him about Galloway. Yeah, we'll ask him. Uh-huh. And, uh, he had, he had a pretty good band. He had Frankie Doosen on trombone.
Yeah. And, uh, Joe Welch on the violin.

Joe Welch, he was a good drummer, but he played violin too, see. Oh, I see. Yeah. In that time, Galloway was getting plenty of work too, you know. Uh-huh. But, a whole lot of country work out of, up, all up the Southern Pacific, TP, all up there. Oh, yeah. A lot of country jobs, just people used to, you know, hire bands that go up in the country there. Yeah. And that kept him busy all the time. Always going in the country, see, band. But he kept busy, though.
